		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">(19)&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Employee and Non&#8209;Employee Director Stock and Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The 2007 Omnibus Equity Compensation Plan (the &#x201C;2007 Plan&#x201D;) was approved by the Company&#x2019;s stockholders and became effective on May&nbsp;8, 2007 (the &#x201C;Effective Date&#x201D;) and was last amended and restated effective June 8, 2017. As of the Effective Date, the Amended and Restated Investment Technology Group,&nbsp;Inc. Directors&#x2019; Retainer Fee Subplan (the &#x201C;Directors&#x2019; Retainer Fee Subplan&#x201D;) and the Amended and Restated Investment Technology Group,&nbsp;Inc. Directors&#x2019; Equity Subplan (the &#x201C;Directors&#x2019; Equity Subplan,&#x201D; and collectively with the Directors&#x2019; Retainer Fee Subplan, the &#x201C;Subplans&#x201D;) were merged with and into the 2007 Plan. Since the Effective Date, the Subplans have continued to be, and shall continue to be, in effect as subplans of the 2007 Plan and grants and/or deferrals may continue to be made. In October 2008, the Compensation Committee of the Company's Board of Directors adopted the Equity Deferral Award Program, another subplan under the 2007 Plan. This subplan, last amended and restated on January 23, 2017, is now known as the Variable Compensation Stock Unit Award Program Subplan, and continues to be a subplan under the 2007 Plan (the &#x201C;VCSUA Subplan&#x201D;).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2017, there were 3,123,105 shares of common stock remaining available for issuance under the 2007 Plan. Shares of common stock which are attributable to awards which have expired, terminated, cash settled or been canceled or forfeited during any calendar year are generally available for issuance or use in connection with future awards. Shares of common stock surrendered in payment of the exercise price of a stock option and shares withheld or surrendered for payment of taxes are not available for re-issuance under the 2007 Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Options outstanding as of December 31, 2017 that have been granted under the 2007 Plan are exercisable on dates ranging through January 2024. The 2007 Plan will remain in effect until June 10, 2025, unless terminated, or extended, by the Board of Directors with the approval of the Company&#x2019;s stockholders. After this date, no further awards shall be granted pursuant to the 2007 Plan, but previously&#8209;granted awards will remain outstanding in accordance with their applicable terms and conditions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In January 2006, the Board of Directors adopted the Directors&#x2019; Equity Subplan which became effective January&nbsp;1, 2006 and merged into the 2007 Plan as referenced above. The Directors&#x2019; Equity Subplan was last amended and restated on January 23, 2017. The Directors&#x2019; Equity Subplan provides for the grant of restricted stock unit awards to non&#8209;employee directors of the Company. Under the Directors&#x2019; Equity Subplan, a newly appointed non&#8209;employee director will be granted restricted stock unit awards valued at $100,000 at, or shortly after, the time of appointment to the Board of Directors. Such initial restricted stock unit awards will vest annually in three equal installments, beginning on the first anniversary of the date of grant so long as the director has continued to serve on the Board of Directors from the grant date to the applicable vesting date. In addition, non&#8209;employee directors are granted restricted stock unit awards annually on the day of each of the Company&#x2019;s annual meetings of stockholders at which directors are elected or reelected by the Company&#x2019;s stockholders. The value of these annual restricted stock unit awards is determined by the Compensation Committee.&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently, the value of restricted stock unit awards granted to the Chairman of the Board of Directors is $120,000 and the value of restricted stock unit awards granted to the other non-employee directors is $80,000. Such annual restricted stock unit awards vest in full on the day immediately preceding the Company&#x2019;s next </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the 2007 Plan, the Company is permitted to grant time&#8209;based stock options, in addition to performance-based option awards to employees and directors. In 2016, the Company granted time-based options for 196,851 shares to the Company&#x2019;s new Chief Executive Officer.&nbsp;&nbsp;These stock options have an eight-year term and vest annually in three equal installments, beginning on the first anniversary of the grant date, if the Chief Executive Officer remains continuously employed by the Company, and is in good standing on, each applicable vesting date. The Company did not grant any option awards under the 2007 Plan during 2015 or 2017. The Company recognizes share&#8209;based compensation expense (see Note&nbsp;2, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font><font style="display:inline;">) for time&#8209;based option awards over the vesting period.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">For the years ended December 31, 2017 and 2016, the Company recorded share-based compensation expense of $0.3 million and $0.3 million, respectively, related to outstanding stock options, which had no income tax benefit in 2017 and was offset by a related income tax benefit of $0.1 million in 2016. For the year ended December 31, 2015, the Company recorded no share-based compensation expense related to outstanding stock options.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">There were 65,630 stock options currently exercisable at December 31, 2017. The weighted average remaining contractual term of stock options currently exercisable is 6.0 years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">All of the stock options outstanding at December 31, 2017 were time&#8209;based.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Prior to the adoption of ASU 2016-09, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting</font><font style="display:inline;">, the provision for income taxes excluded excess current tax benefits related to the exercise of stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective January 1, 2017, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">all subsequent excess tax benefits and deficiencies are recognized in the statement of operations as an increase or decrease in income taxes when the awards vest or are settled</font><font style="display:inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;See discussion in Note 2, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies.&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">During 2017, there were no exercises of stock options and therefore no corresponding current tax </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">81</font>

		</p>

During 2016, the exercise of 42,655 stock options gave rise to an excess current tax benefit of $0.1 million. During 2015, the exercise of 71,455 stock options gave rise to an excess current tax benefit of less than $0.1 million, however, this amount was offset by a tax shortfall on exercises and cancellations totaling $0.6 million.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The total intrinsic value for outstanding and exercisable stock options at December 31, 2017 was $0.6 million and $0.2 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2017, there was $0.3 million of unrecognized compensation costs related to outstanding stock options.&nbsp;&nbsp;These costs are expected to be recognized ratably over a weighted average period of approximately 1.0 year. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the 2007 Plan, the Company is permitted to grant restricted stock unit awards to employees. Generally, and except for awards granted under the VCSUA Subplan, restricted stock unit awards vest in one of the following manners: (a) one-third on the second anniversary of the grant date and two-thirds on the third anniversary of the grant date, (b) cliff vesting on the third anniversary of the grant date, (c) for new hire awards only, vesting terms that closely parallel the vesting terms of any awards that the new hire will forfeit upon joining the Company, except that no such new hire award or portion thereof shall vest prior to the one-year anniversary of the date of grant unless otherwise permitted by the 2007 Plan, or (d) serial vest on each of the second, third and fourth anniversaries of the date of grant so long as the award recipient is employed on the applicable vesting date and the 90-day average of the Company&#x2019;s common stock price preceding each of the vesting dates is greater than the 90-day average of the Company&#x2019;s common stock price preceding the grant date (market-based restricted stock units). Accordingly, not all restricted stock units awarded will vest and be delivered. The Company recognizes share-based compensation expense (see Note 2, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font><font style="display:inline;">) over the vesting period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the VCSUA Subplan, beginning in January 2017, each eligible participant was granted a number of basic stock units on the date the year-end variable compensation is communicated to participants equal to (i) the amount by which the participant&#x2019;s variable compensation is reduced as determined by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors, divided by (ii) the fair market value of a share of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the date of grant. Prior to January 2017, the basic stock units were granted on the date the year-end cash bonus was paid to participants.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, each participant is granted an additional number of matching stock units on the date of grant equal to 10% of the number of time-based or market-based basic stock units granted. Basic stock units under the VCSUA Subplan that are time-based typically vest in equal annual installments on each of the first, second and third anniversaries of the date of grant, if the participant remains continuously employed by the Company, and is in good standing on, each applicable vesting date. Time-based matching stock units will vest 100% on the third anniversary of the date of grant, if the participant remains continuously employed by the Company through, and is in good standing on, such vesting date. Basic units under the VCSUA Subplan that are market-based (which were granted in February 2014 to members of senior management) vest in equal installments on each of the second, third and fourth anniversaries of the date of grant so long as the award recipient is employed on the applicable vesting date and the 90&#8209;day average of the Company&#x2019;s common stock price preceding each of the vesting dates is greater than the 90&#8209;day average of the Company&#x2019;s common stock price preceding the grant date. Matching stock units on market-based awards will vest 100% on the fourth anniversary of the date of grant so long as the award recipient is employed on the applicable vesting date and the 90&#8209;day average of the Company&#x2019;s common stock price preceding the vesting date is greater than the 90&#8209;day average of the Company&#x2019;s common stock price preceding the grant date. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has also issued to members of its senior management basic stock units under the VCSUA that vest in one of the following manners: (a) for awards granted in February 2015, in equal installments on each of the first, second, and third anniversaries of the date of grant based upon the level of the Company&#x2019;s adjusted return-on-equity (&#x201C;ROE&#x201D;) achieved for each of the three fiscal years, respectively, that ends immediately prior to the applicable vesting date, (b) for awards granted in February 2016, in equal installments on each of the second and third anniversaries of the date of grant based upon the level of ROE achieved for each of the two fiscal years, respectively, that ends immediately prior to the applicable vesting date (each ROE-based restricted stock units) or (c) for awards granted in February 2017, </font><font style="display:inline;background-color: #FFFFFF;">between January&nbsp;1, 2019 and February&nbsp;5, 2019, the Compensation Committee will determine and certify the extent to </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;background-color: #FFFFFF;">which the basic units have been earned, if at all, based on the levels of revenue and pre-tax margin achieved for the 2018 fiscal year, and such earned basic units shall be divided into two equal installments, with the first installment vesting on February&nbsp;5, 2019 and the second installment vesting on February&nbsp;5, 2020 (performance-based restricted stock units)</font><font style="display:inline;">. In addition to the performance criteria being achieved under each of these awards, the participant must remain continuously employed by the Company through, and be in good standing on, each applicable vesting date. The number of ROE-based restricted basic stock units awarded will be earned in each of the relevant performance periods if the target ROE is achieved at 100% and such number may increase or decrease if the actual ROE achieved is above or below the target ROE. In addition, certain senior employees have received matching ROE-based restricted stock units and such awards vest on the third anniversary of the date of grant based upon the average of the ROE achieved during the three-year period that ends immediately prior to the applicable vesting date. The number of matching ROE-based restricted stock units awarded will be earned if the target average ROE is achieved at 100% and such number may increase or decrease if the actual average ROE achieved is above or below the target average ROE. The number of performance-based restricted stock units earned is determined pursuant to a payout matrix established by the Committee that sets forth a range of payout percentages relative to the Company&#x2019;s actual revenue and pre-tax margin results achieved for the 2018 fiscal year, with each performance metric weighted equally.&nbsp;&nbsp;All vested stock units are settled in shares of ITG common stock within 30&nbsp;days after the date on which such stock units vest.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During 2016, the Company granted two Inducement Awards in conjunction with the hiring of its new Chief Executive Officer, which replaced awards he forfeited at his former employer.&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;background-color: #FFFFFF;">Under the first inducement award, the Chief Executive Officer was granted 135,353 restricted stock units that vest in three equal annual installments beginning on the first anniversary of the grant date.&nbsp; Under the second inducement award, the Chief Executive Officer was granted 156,051 restricted stock units which vested on the following vesting dates: (i)&nbsp;38% vested on January&nbsp;31, 2016 and were subject to a 12-month holding requirement; (ii)&nbsp;41% vested on January&nbsp;31, 2017; and (iii)&nbsp;the remaining 21% vested on January&nbsp;31, 2018.</font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On May 27, 2016, the Company sold Investment Research (See Note 4, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Divestitures and Acquisitions</font><font style="display:inline;">).&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the closing of the transaction, the Company accelerated the vesting of 226,802 restricted stock unit awards held by employees that were part of Investment Research and are included in the table above.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost to modify the vesting schedule of these shares resulted in an expense reversal of $0.7 million that is included as part of the gain in other revenues in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December 22, 2015, the Company sold its energy research operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the closing of the transaction, the Company accelerated the vesting of 113,718 restricted stock unit awards held by employees that were part of the energy research business and are included in the table above.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost to modify the vesting schedule of these shares was $1.4 million and is included as a direct cost of the sale that reduced the gain included in other revenues in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2017, there was $25.8&nbsp;million of total unrecognized compensation cost related to outstanding restricted stock unit awards. These costs are expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of approximately 1.3&nbsp;years. During 2017, restricted stock unit awards with a fair value of approximately $21.9&nbsp;million vested.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Prior to the adoption of ASU 2016-09, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting</font><font style="display:inline;">, the provision for income taxes excluded excess current tax benefits related to the vesting of restricted share units.&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective January 1, 2017 all subsequent excess tax benefits and deficiencies are recognized in the statement of operations. See discussion in Note 2, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For the year ended December 31, 2017, the excess tax benefits totaled $1.5 million and tax shortfalls (arising from cancellations or deficits due to the vest date fair market value being less than the grant date fair market value) were $0.1 million. For the year ended December 31, 2016, the excess tax benefits totaled $0.8&nbsp;million while tax shortfalls were $0.7&nbsp;million. For the year ended December 31, 2015, the excess tax benefits totaled $2.9 million while tax shortfalls were $0.3 million. For the years 2016 and 2015, such tax benefits are reflected as an increase in additional paid-in capital while tax shortfalls arising from the tax deduction being less than the cumulative book compensation cost is reflected as a decrease in additional paid-in capital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the 2007 Plan and the VCSUA Subplan, the Company is permitted to grant phantom share awards. Phantom share awards vest like any other award granted under the 2007 Plan and VCSUA Subplan as described above and are settled in cash. The Company recognizes share&#8209;based compensation expense (see Note&nbsp;2, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font><font style="display:inline;">) over the applicable vesting period. For the years ended December 31, 2016 and 2015, the Company recorded share&#8209;based compensation expense of $0.1&nbsp;million and $2.2&nbsp;million, respectively, related to phantom share awards offset by related tax benefits of less than $0.1&nbsp;million and $0.8&nbsp;million, respectively.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">ITG Employee and Non&#8209;Employee Director Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">All U.S. employees are eligible to participate in the Investment Technology Group,&nbsp;Inc. Retirement Savings Plan (&#x201C;RSP&#x201D;). The RSP applies to all eligible compensation up to the Internal Revenue Service annual maximum which was $270,000 during 2017. Since January&nbsp;1, 2012, the Company matching contribution applies to 50% of voluntary employee contributions, on a maximum of 4% of eligible compensation per year. The Company may still make discretionary contributions based on consolidated profits. Most of the Company&#x2019;s international employees are eligible to participate in similar defined contribution plans. The costs for these benefits were approximately $4.3&nbsp;million, $4.4&nbsp;million, and $4.9&nbsp;million in 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively, and are included in compensation and employee benefits in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In November 1997, the Board of Directors approved the ITG Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#x201C;ESPP&#x201D;), an employee stock purchase plan qualified under Section&nbsp;423 of the Internal Revenue Code. The ESPP became effective February&nbsp;1, 1998 and allows all full&#8209;time employees to purchase shares of ITG common stock at a 15% discount. In accordance with the provisions of ASC 718, the ESPP is compensatory. The Company recorded share&#8209;based compensation expense related to the ESPP of $0.3 million, $0.4 million and $0.3 million for the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During 2017, each non&#8209;employee director received a general Board retainer fee of $70,000, with the exception of the Chairman who received $105,000. Each non-employee director was also eligible to receive a Committee Chair retainer fee and Committee member retainer fee depending on their role on the Board&#x2019;s Committees. Under the Directors&#x2019; Retainer Fee Subplan, which was adopted in 2002, these retainer fees are payable, at the election of each director, either in (i)&nbsp;cash, (ii)&nbsp;Company common stock with a value equal to the retainer fee on the grant date or (iii)&nbsp;under a deferred compensation plan which provides deferred share units with a value equal to the retainer fee on the grant date which convert to freely sellable shares when the director retires from the Board of Directors. Directors who chose common stock or deferred share units, in the aggregate, received 11,115 units or shares, 12,363 units or shares, and 13,846 units or shares in 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively. At December 31, 2017, there were 130,940 deferred share units outstanding, of which 20,485 shares were vested and deferred in 2017. The cost of the Directors&#x2019; Retainer Fee Subplan including share based awards and cash fees was approximately $0.8 million, $0.8 million, and $1.2 million in 2017, 2016 and 2015, respectively, and is included in other general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Legal Matters</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times;background-color: #FFFFFF;">On January 12, 2017, the Company reached a final settlement with the SEC to resolve the SEC&#x2019;s inquiry into ITG Inc.&#x2019;s activity with respect to pre-released American Depositary Receipts (&#x201C;ADRs&#x201D;), </font><font style="display:inline;">substantially all of which related to ITG Inc.&#x2019;s matched-book operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;ITG Inc.&#x2019;s activity in pre-released ADRs was discontinued in the fourth quarter of 2014, with all outstanding transactions completely wound down by the end of 2014.&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times;background-color: #FFFFFF;"> According to the terms of the settlement, the Company paid an aggregate amount of $24.5&nbsp;million in January 2017, which includes disgorgement of $15.1 million, prejudgment interest of $1.9 million and a civil monetary penalty of $7.5&nbsp;million. The Company had fully reserved the </font><font style="display:inline;">$24.5 million as of December 31, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company is not a party to any pending legal proceedings other than claims and lawsuits arising in the ordinary course of business, except a putative class action lawsuit and a derivative action have been filed with respect to the Company and certain of its current and former directors and/or executives in connection with the Company&#x2019;s announcement of the SEC matter described in the following paragraph (and other related actions could be filed).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On August 12, 2015, the Company reached a final settlement with the SEC in connection with the SEC&#x2019;s investigation into a proprietary trading pilot operated within AlterNet for sixteen months in 2010 through mid-2011. The investigation was focused on customer disclosures, Form ATS regulatory filings and customer information controls relating to the pilot&#x2019;s trading activity, which included (a) crossing against sell-side clients in POSIT and (b) violations of Company policy and procedures by a former employee. These violations principally involved information breaches for a period of several months in 2010 regarding sell-side parent orders flowing into ITG&#x2019;s algorithms and executions by all customers in non-POSIT markets that were not otherwise available to ITG clients.&nbsp;&nbsp;According to the terms of the settlement, the Company paid an aggregate amount of $20.3 million, representing a civil penalty of $18 million, disgorgement of approximately $2.1 million in trading revenues and prejudgment interest of approximately $0.25 million.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In connection with the announcement of the SEC investigation regarding AlterNet, two putative class action lawsuits were filed with respect to the Company and certain of its current and former executives and have since been consolidated into a single action captioned&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">In re Investment Technology Group, Inc.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Securities Litigation</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The complaint alleges, among other things, that the defendants made material misrepresentations or omitted to disclose material facts concerning, among other subjects, the matters that were the subject of the SEC settlement regarding AlterNet and the SEC investigation that led to the SEC settlement. The complaint seeks an unspecified amount of damages under the federal securities laws. On April 26, 2017, the court granted in part and denied in part the Company&#x2019;s motion to dismiss the complaint</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Verdana;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">and granted the plaintiff leave to file a motion to amend its complaint. On June 12, 2017, the plaintiff filed a motion to amend its complaint against certain of the individual defendants who were dismissed from the case in the court&#x2019;s April opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On November 27, 2015, a purported shareholder of the Company filed a shareholder derivative action captioned&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Watterson v.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Gasser et al.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;against eleven current or former officers and directors of the Company in the Supreme Court for the State of New York. The Company is named as a nominal defendant, and the plaintiff purports to seek recovery on its behalf. The complaint generally alleges that the individual defendants breached their fiduciary duties to the Company in connection with the matters that were the subject of the SEC settlement regarding AlterNet.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">While the Company cannot predict the outcome of these lawsuits, the Company intends to defend them as appropriate. No reserve has been established for these lawsuits since the Company is unable to provide a reasonable estimate of any potential liability given the stage of such proceedings. The Company believes, based on information currently available, that the outcome of these lawsuits, individually or in the aggregate, will not likely have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position.&nbsp;&nbsp;In light of the inherent uncertainties of such proceedings, an adverse outcome of one or more of such proceedings may have a material impact on the results of operations for any particular period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In addition to the above proceedings, the Company&#x2019;s broker-dealer subsidiaries are subject to, or involved in, investigations and other proceedings by government agencies and self-regulatory organizations, with respect to which the Company is cooperating. Such investigations and other proceedings may result in judgments, settlements, fines, disgorgements, penalties, injunctions or other relief.&nbsp; Given the inherent uncertainties and the current stage of these </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Lease Commitments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has entered into lease and sublease agreements with third parties for certain offices and equipment, which expire at various dates through 2030. Rent expense for each of the years ended December 31, 2017, 2016 and 2015 was $11.8&nbsp;million, $12.7 million and $12.4&nbsp;million, respectively, and is recorded in occupancy and equipment expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. The Company recognizes rent expense for escalation clauses, rent holidays, leasehold improvement incentives and other concessions using the straight&#8209;line method over the minimum lease term. Minimum future rental commitments under non&#8209;cancelable operating leases follow (dollars in thousands):</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%;"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" align="center" style="border-collapse:collapse;width: 80.00%;margin-left:0pt;">
			<tr>

			<font style="display:inline;">The accounting policies of the reportable segments are the same as those described in Note&nbsp;2, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font><font style="display:inline;">. &nbsp;The Company allocates resources to, and evaluates the performance of, its reportable segments based on income or loss before income tax expense (benefit). Consistent with the Company&#x2019;s resource allocation and operating performance evaluation approach, the effects of inter-segment activities are eliminated except in limited circumstances where certain technology related costs are allocated to a segment to support that segment&#x2019;s revenue producing activities. Commissions and fees revenue for trade executions and commission share revenues are principally attributed to each segment based upon the location of execution of the related transaction except that commissions and fees for trade executions by Canadian clients in the U.S. market are attributed to the Canadian </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

Recurring revenues are principally attributed based upon the location of the client using the respective service.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">There were no changes in the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the quarter ended December 31, 2017 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The management of ITG is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. ITG&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed under the supervision of ITG&#x2019;s chief executive and chief financial officers, and affected by ITG&#x2019;s board of directors, management and other personnel, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of ITG&#x2019;s financial statements for external reporting purposes in accordance with U.S.&nbsp;GAAP and includes policies and procedures that (i)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of ITG, (ii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S.&nbsp;GAAP, and that receipts and expenditures of ITG are being made only in accordance with authorizations of ITG&#x2019;s management and directors and (iii)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of ITG&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with policies and procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Management assessed the effectiveness of ITG&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017. In making this assessment, management used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Internal Control&#x2014;Integrated Framework (2013)</font><font style="display:inline;">. Based on its assessment and those criteria, management has concluded that ITG maintained effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The effectiveness of ITG&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017 has been audited by KPMG&nbsp;LLP, ITG&#x2019;s independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report on the following page, which expressed an unqualified opinion on the effectiveness of ITG&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2017.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders<br />Investment Technology Group,&nbsp;Inc.: </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Opinion on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We have audited Investment Technology Group,&nbsp;Inc. and Subsidiaries&nbsp;&nbsp;(the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2017, based on criteria established in</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;"> Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework (2013)</font><font style="display:inline;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2017, based on criteria established in </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Internal Control &#x2013; Integrated Framework (2013)</font><font style="display:inline;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#x201C;PCAOB&#x201D;), the consolidated statement of financial condition of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2017 and 2016, the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive (loss) income, change in stockholders&#x2019; equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December&nbsp;31, 2017, and the related notes (collectively, the consolidated financial statements), and our report dated February 28, 2018</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">expressed an unqualified opinion on those consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Basis for Opinion </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audit also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Definition and Limitations of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times;font-size:10pt;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%;"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" align="center" style="border-collapse:collapse;width: 100.00%;margin-left:0pt;">
